html:
Nayarit marks the land of western Mexico between the Pacific coast and the Sierra Madre, now the state of Nayarit, in the years of the Spanish conquest. Its peoples included the Cora of the mountains, the Huichol, and the farming lordships of the coast around Tepic.

In 1530 and 1531 the brutal conquistador Nuño Beltrán de Guzmán marched through the region, burning towns and enslaving people, and founded the province of Nueva Galicia. The peoples of the west rose against the Spanish in the Mixtón War of 1540 to 1542, which was put down only with a large army.

The Cora of the Sierra del Nayar stayed independent in their mountains until 1722, long after the rest of Mexico had fallen; they kept their own religion and a sacred shrine of an ancestor ruler, the Nayar, after whom the region is named.
